q8.answer: Nothing cancels it. It keeps waiting for approval and the window. After it takes the production lock, it reads /deploy/production/current_tag. If its SHA equals that tag or is an ancestor of it, it ends quietly as superseded, with no deploy and no alert. Otherwise it proceeds. The staging run of the newer merge does not by itself supersede it. Supersession is only checked against what is deployed in each environment's current_tag.

q9.answer: Outside the window it waits with no lock held until the next window start (Mon to Thu 09:00 to 15:00 UTC). Then it takes the production-deploy lock and queues behind any other production deploy. After getting the lock it rechecks the window. If the window has closed, it releases the lock and waits again. It then checks for supersession before running deploy.sh canary.

q10.answer: The canary's 5xx ratio over the last minute is measured, using the Prometheus query from environments.md. The pipeline queries it every 30 seconds for 15 minutes, which is 30 samples. Any single sample above 1% fails the run. No data is ignored for the first 2 minutes, and after that 2 consecutive no-data samples fail the run. A failure runs canary-off and announces in #deploys.

q11.answer: I did not decide this. The document says the CI approval job is restricted to release-approvers and records who approved and when. It does not specify any notification to approvers, such as a Slack post when a run starts waiting. It also does not specify what information the approver sees, such as the SHA, diff, or staging smoke results. I relied on the CI's built-in approval job and left the rest undefined.

q12.answer: The pipeline does not run rollback after a failed deploy script, in staging or production. The scripts write the SSM tags only after the rollout succeeds, so after a partial failure current_tag still names the old version. rollback would restore previous_tag, which is one version too far back. Instead the run fails, #deploys is told the cluster may be mid-rollout, and a person inspects it. The next successful deploy corrects SSM. Rollback runs only after a smoke-test failure, when the deploy succeeded and the tags are correct. For a production stable rollout failure there is no automatic rollback. The run goes to canary-off and failure. I did not design a way to automatically return to a known image in that case, only to leave it for a person.
